transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

They sent me here from the station. I kept moving the airway bags into this pattern—I knew it was the right one—and saying the dispatch numbers out loud. My lieutenant told me to stop, but I couldn't step away. It felt like the whole bay would go bad if I broke the sequence.
Did this need to arrange the bags start happening after a particularly traumatic or distressing call?
I’m not sure. I can’t point to one call that started it. It just became something I felt I had to do.
Deep down, do you feel that moving the bags realistically has the power to prevent something bad from happening, or do you recognize that the thought doesn't make logical sense?
It feels like it really matters. I knew the bags had to be in that pattern, and if I stopped or changed it, the whole bay was going to go bad. I couldn't just walk away from it.
Do you ever hear voices, noises, or whispers that other people around you can't hear?
I haven’t noticed hearing voices or whispers that other people can’t hear.
Do you ever feel that people are watching, following, or plotting against you?

Yeah. I know the injury review people and some of the supervisors have been watching me through the station cameras. They’ve been changing my triage notes too, making it look like I’m unsafe, even though they tell me it’s just routine paperwork.
Have you ever felt like thoughts were being placed directly into your head, or taken out of your mind against your will?

No, not exactly thoughts being put in or taken out. It’s more that I know they’re watching me through the station cameras and altering my triage notes to make me look unsafe, even though they call it routine paperwork.
Have you noticed a significant drop in your motivation, energy, or ability to take care of your everyday responsibilities?

Yeah. Most days I just sit in my apartment. There’s trash in the corner and food still in the fridge, and I don’t cook or call the guys to play basketball like I used to. I just can’t get myself to care enough to start anything.
About how long have you been dealing with these problems, such as feeling watched and struggling to get things done?
About eight months, I think. It started after I hurt my shoulder and ribs during that ambulance transfer.
